reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents Texas Roadhouse coupons and a branded newsletter signup connected to promotional offers. The requests for personal and household details are noted, but the available video evidence describes no deceptive conduct or unsafe data use.

citations.quote: Coupons for Texas Roadhouse can help you save money on steaks, baby back ribs, a variety of beer, and many other Roadhouse favorites.
Also available on the restaurant's official site is the company's newsletter, which will give you a free appetizer coupon just for signing up.
you can gain access to the promotional information and coupons contained in the company newsletter, such as $5.00 off an order of $20 or more.

opening.argument: The central pitch links a low-barrier reward to a concrete registration flow. Viewers are told that signing up for the newsletter will provide a free appetizer coupon, while the signup page requests an email address, name, birthdate, favorite location, home ZIP code, and household information. That is not merely discussion of coupons: it is a solicitation in which submitting personal details is the route to an advertised benefit. The video also presents a $5 discount tied to a minimum purchase, reinforcing the pattern of an attractive reward conditioned on viewer action.

citations.quote: the company's newsletter, which will give you a free appetizer coupon just for signing up
such as $5.00 off an order of $20 or more

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the offer a restaurant promotion does not resolve the solicitation concern. The evidence specifically connects a free appetizer to signing up, and the signup screen shows that the requested information goes beyond an email address. The reference statement acknowledges those requests but offers no evidence establishing how the collected details are used or why all of them are necessary for the promised benefit.

citations.quote: which will give you a free appetizer coupon just for signing up

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The signup page does show requested fields, but that alone does not show deception, misuse, or an unavailable reward. The accompanying description consistently identifies the benefit as a newsletter coupon and describes the discount as promotional information, including $5 off a qualifying order. The cited material establishes a conditional promotion, not a false promise or unsafe data practice.

citations.quote: the company's newsletter, which will give you a free appetizer coupon just for signing up
promotional information and coupons contained in the company newsletter

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: the video directs viewers to external deal and coupon destinations, advertises a free appetizer for signing up, and displays a form requesting identifying and household-related details. The on-screen form includes birthdate, location preference, ZIP code, and whether the viewer has children aged 12 or under. The promise of “delicious gifts and other fun stuff” delivered by email is therefore paired with broad data collection, while the video also promotes additional coupon-search routes. That combination makes the reward pathway materially more questionable than an ordinary coupon image alone.

citations.quote: Ask Texas Roadhouse for a deal: http://askforadeal.com

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening focuses on the restaurant branding and coupon language, but those points do not answer the combined risk signals. The evidence shows a reward-oriented signup form collecting birthdate, ZIP code, location, and child-related information; it does not show that these details are required for a legitimate coupon or explain the handling of that information. External deal links further shift the viewer from informational content toward participation.

citations.quote: Ask Texas Roadhouse for a deal: http://askforadeal.com

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The visible fields establish what the form asks for, but not that the offer is deceptive or that the information is mishandled. The description identifies the signup as a company newsletter and describes ordinary sources such as newspapers, magazines, and Facebook for coupons. External links and a reward offer can exist in normal advertising without proving a scam.

citations.quote: Customers can register to receive the Texas Roadhouse newsletter
Many food and dining magazines as well as newspapers, or periodicals, may have coupons for Texas Roadhouse available

opening.argument: Although presented as help finding discounts, the video functions as a promotional funnel. It showcases the restaurant, directs viewers to coupon sources, highlights a “Become a Texas Roadie VIP” signup, and displays a free-appetizer offer alongside a form for viewer information. The repeated movement from restaurant content to registration and deal-request links makes the practical purpose participation in promotional channels, not neutral consumer education. The branded presentation and reward language strengthen that solicitation framing.

citations.quote: Ask For a Deal allows you to request deals and find coupons for your favorite products and services.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The label “coupons” describes the subject, not the function of the video. The frames prominently present VIP enrollment and a free appetizer, while the description tells viewers to request deals and find coupons through an external service. Those calls to participate are the operative content, so branding and ordinary restaurant imagery do not make the presentation merely informational.

citations.quote: Ask For a Deal allows you to request deals and find coupons for your favorite products and services.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The video can both explain where coupons may be found and promote a legitimate restaurant newsletter. Its text explicitly states that the purpose is to help viewers find coupons and identifies the newsletter as the source of promotional information and coupons. Restaurant imagery and branded signup screens support ordinary promotion; they do not establish a deceptive role or a false benefit.

citations.quote: The purpose of this video is to help you find them.
promotional information and coupons contained in the company newsletter
You can also follow Texas Roadhouse on Facebook for news, promotions, and the occasional discount or redeemable coupon
